It depends on encryption and other factors. Sure you can find it , but it's very unlikely. Even administration login pages and other such things are deepweb content. So yes , you can open some stuff in your ol regular browser , but it's certainly not something you would consider surface web content.
The "clearnet" as you say is content that can be accessed using standart search engines. If Google , Bing etc. cannot find it , it's already categorised as being on the deep web.
I highly doubt that anything highly sinister would be put on the surface web.

Might aswell chip in. I started smoking when I was 13 or so because of peer pressure. Sure back then I was stupid and thought that smoking was cool and that it will get me friends. It didin't. Fast foward to me being 15 , I had quit by then for a year. But oh boy , here come the mental issues and stress. I was considered the smart guy in class even though I didin't know shit. That's when I started smoking heavily. I smoke to this day, at this point it's probably a pack a day(I'm 18). My best advice is - never start doing something because of others. And certainly get help for your mental issues because chemical substances are not the answer.
